facts.fact: The Ministry of Social Affairs presented the first deliverable of the unified social registry (RSUG) on 29 July 2026, with the stated aim of setting up the registry.

The ministry and World Bank experts reviewed progress on implementing the Registre social unique, a centralised national database meant to identify the most vulnerable households, at a 7 May 2026 meeting.
Gabon finalised the technical work on the Registre Social Unique at a closing workshop on 28 August 2025, a database to target aid and avoid duplication.

systems.owner: Ministry of Women, Family and Child Protection

facts.fact: The Minister of Social Affairs officially received the strategic deliverables of the Registre social unique du Gabon on 29 July 2026, under the Gabon Digital programme, marking the start of setting up the registry.

note: The RSU is described as to be deployed; the article states no procurement, pilot or population, only a six-day manual-drafting workshop opened 14 October 2026.

facts.fact: The amended Digital Gabon financing agreement (effective 2 September 2026) refers to the existing social protection beneficiary registry managed by CNAM-GS and finances improving it.

note: Workshop set bases of a future registry; two-year implementation planned, not procured, piloted or populated.

facts.fact: TechReviewAfrica reports ANINF's roadmap for the Unified Social Registry (RSU) starts with development of a specialized social protection information system, in three implementation phases agreed with the Minister of Women, Family and Child Protection and World Bank representatives.

note: Registry is planned: developer to be recruited by Feb 2027, service by Apr 2028; no procurement, pilot or population stated.
